title: Project 2025 Proposes Broader DOJ Leak Investigations and Journalist-Source Searches
description_short: A 2024 Truthout report says Project 2025 calls for wider leak investigations, fewer limits on access to journalists' communications, and more staff to identify sources.
description_medium: Truthout writer Chip Gibbons reported on October 27, 2024, that Project 2025 asks DOJ to use all tools to investigate leaks, repeal guidelines limiting access to journalists’ communications, and add counterintelligence and security personnel to identify sources for prosecution. The article discusses proposed policy, not actions implemented by the second Trump administration.
description_long: Truthout published Chip Gibbons’s opinion piece on October 27, 2024, before the presidential election. It describes Project 2025 as a proposed governing plan and quotes its call for the Justice Department to “use all of the tools at its disposal to investigate leaks.” Gibbons reports that the plan proposes repealing guidelines that limit when law enforcement can obtain journalists’ communications and prioritizing additional counterintelligence and security personnel to identify journalists’ sources for prosecution. The article places these recommendations in the debate over Espionage Act cases and press protections, and quotes former FBI agent Mike German criticizing the adequacy of whistleblower safeguards. It also contrasts the proposal with Attorney General Merrick Garland’s 2022 policy restricting access to reporters’ records. A Kettering Foundation article by Joel Simon, dated October 30, 2024, frames potential effects on media freedom as a risk. These 2024 sources document proposals and analysis; they do not establish that the proposed measures were later implemented.
subcategory: Press Freedom Elimination and Journalist Persecution

preserved_fields.title: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
preserved_fields.description_short: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
preserved_fields.subcategory: Press Freedom Elimination and Journalist Persecution
preserved_fields.description_long: Donald Trump systematically eliminated government press credentials and media access by revoking accreditation for journalists who reported critically on administration policies while implementing Project 2025's plan to 'use all tools at disposal to investigate leaks' and prosecute reporters' sources under the Espionage Act for routine newsgathering activities. The comprehensive press freedom destruction represented Trump's implementation of authoritarian media control that transformed government transparency from democratic principle into criminal offense, with journalists facing prosecution for reporting on government misconduct while losing access to official proceedings and information sources. The credential elimination included ending White House press briefings, restricting congressional access, eliminating agency briefings, and denying accreditation to independent journalists while providing exclusive access to conservative media outlets that promoted administration propaganda rather than factual reporting. Trump's media targeting violated First Amendment press freedom protections by using federal law enforcement to investigate journalists while treating routine news reporting as criminal activity subject to surveillance and prosecution under anti-terrorism and espionage statutes designed for foreign agents rather than domestic media. The press access destruction created what journalism advocates called return to authoritarian media control where government information became propaganda distribution rather than public accountability, with independent journalism facing systematic persecution through credential denial and source prosecution. The journalist targeting represented Project 2025's vision of media controlled by government loyalty rather than press freedom, transforming news reporting from public service into criminal activity while eliminating transparency mechanisms that had historically exposed government corruption and held officials accountable for violations of law and public trust.

notes: Focused source checks: Truthout (Chip Gibbons, October 27, 2024; HTTP 200) quotes Project 2025's leak-investigation recommendation and describes proposals to repeal DOJ limits on access to journalists' communications and add counterintelligence/security staff to find sources. Kettering Foundation's October 30, 2024 article by Joel Simon describes potential media-freedom risks; its page returned HTTP 200 once with article metadata/summary and HTTP 403 on a later request. PEN America's linked page returned HTTP 403. The new text is scoped to the documented proposal and analysis; these sources do not establish implementation.
proposed_correction: Describe the cited proposals as proposals unless a dated U.S. credential revocation, prosecution or source investigation is documented. Remove claims that briefings ended or reporters were prosecuted absent supporting records.
